markdown_report:
At 10% research progress, prioritize a small diagnostic improvement that can test hypotheses before spending the training budget.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics has a 14.95% sampled training misranking rate, versus 3.03% for Movies_and_TV. This supports category-specific investigation but does not establish validation performance. (2) Existing deletion probes compact positions. Their responses therefore combine removed content with positional changes. (3) User feedback distinguishes broad relatedness from current usefulness. Histories and item text can support hypotheses about this distinction, but cannot establish purpose, compatibility, or dislike.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Recency and positional mechanisms can differ [1,2]. Consequently, recent-history sensitivity needs controls that preserve edited positions. (2) Sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog rankings [3]. Diagnostic catalog ranks must remain separate from the pinned validation objective. (3) Personalized judges show limited preference agreement [4]. Missing evidence should produce an unresolved judgment rather than rejection.

These insights define three directions: isolate sequence mechanisms; audit ranking under different candidate sets; and attach evidence and uncertainty to semantic judgments.

| Direction | Existing method | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sequence mechanisms | Compacted deletions | Position-preserving matched replacements | Edits remain synthetic |
| Ranking reliability | Sampled training margins | Fixed full-catalog rank changes | Sensitivity is not accuracy |
| Semantic evidence | Qualitative user feedback | Text-supported hypotheses with abstention | Intent remains unobserved |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each out of 10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Matched replacement probe — 5/7/4.** Originality: combines established controls, but extends the current adapter. Potential: separates important confounds, but cannot establish intent. Difficulty: uses existing scoring hooks, but sparse matching requires care [1,2].
- **Candidate-set disagreement audit — 4/7/4.** Originality: established ranking analysis, with useful category stratification. Potential: exposes misleading margins, but may not predict benchmark gains. Difficulty: straightforward scoring, with substantial catalog cost [3].
- **Evidence-backed unresolved-case rubric — 5/6/6.** Originality: adapts selective judgment, but largely concerns annotation. Potential: improves interpretation, but needs independent labels. Difficulty: simple schema, costly validation [4].

**Selected idea: matched replacement probe.** Replace one recent or older nonpadding item without moving other positions. Match donor items using training frequency, training transition counts, and optional title/description TF-IDF similarity; report matching residuals and unmatched cases. Preserve timestamps as fixed model inputs where applicable, documenting that edited histories are synthetic.

For five supplied training users per category, reuse the original unseen-item catalog and five seeded draws. Measure paired top-10 overlap and original-top-10 rank displacement; identity replacements audit correctness. Freeze the model, restore modes and RNG states, and retain `DiagnosisProbe` and its return contract. Treat findings as observational sensitivity. Select any subsequent intervention solely through unchanged four-category macro validation HR@10; no recommendation improvement is claimed.

idea.description: Extend the existing diagnostic adapter with position-preserving matched item replacements to compare model sensitivity to recent and older history content.
idea.motivation: Current deletions change both content and positions. Matched replacements provide a more controlled test of recency dependence while respecting the limited evidence about user purpose and preferences.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and the metrics/metric_definitions return structure. Use view.model in evaluation and inference modes, restoring module flags and Python, NumPy, and torch RNG states afterward. Build donor statistics exclusively from training interactions and permitted titles/descriptions; never access unavailable ratings, categories, prices, stores, or review text. Match within each dataset using log-frequency distance and smoothed transition counts, with optional sparse TF-IDF cosine distance. Exclude padding, the original item, and the user's original history from donors. Use fixed matching tolerances, document match coverage, and skip unmatched contrasts. Hold padding, sequence length, timestamps, and all unedited positions fixed. Use the five supplied users per category without substituting users. Score catalogs in chunks on one GPU and exclude each user's complete original history consistently across edits. Report whether a replacement donor appears in recommendations, since this can affect displacement. Store artifacts beneath the trial directory and retain DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. This proposal changes diagnostics only; future architecture changes must also update the predictor writer. No training, validation, or performance gain is asserted here.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save module modes and RNG states
    enter evaluation mode and inference mode
    build training-only frequency, transition, and optional text statistics
    for each dataset and its five supplied panel users:
        sequence = original padded training history
        candidates = catalog excluding complete original history
        baseline = score(sequence, candidates)
        audit identity replacement against baseline
        for draw in five fixed seeded draws:
            choose recent and older nonpadding positions
            find donors satisfying the same declared matching tolerances
            if either match is unavailable:
                record unmatched contrast; continue
            replace each position separately without compaction
            score both edits against the identical candidate pool
            record top-10 overlap, original-top-10 rank displacement,
                   matching residuals, and donor-entry indicators
        compute paired recent-minus-older changes
    aggregate equally across users within each category
    report counts, exploratory paired intervals, limitations, and cost
    restore modes and RNG states in finally block
    return metrics, metric_definitions

Use unchanged host macro validation HR@10 to select subsequent trained interventions.

originality.positive: Adds matched, position-preserving contrasts to an existing architecture-compatible history-edit adapter.
originality.negative: Matched perturbations and recency probes are established methods; the contribution is a careful task-specific combination.

future_potential.positive: Can motivate targeted, validation-tested recency or positional ablations while making diagnostic confounds explicit.
future_potential.negative: Synthetic replacements may be implausible, and diagnostic sensitivity may fail to predict intervention gains.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses existing representations, scoring hooks, panel selection, and catalog-ranking infrastructure.
code_difficulty.negative: Sparse transition matching, catalog scoring cost, and missing-match handling require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] Measuring Recency Bias
contributions: Introduces a recency diagnostic and reports improvements from reducing excessive recency bias.
limitations: Does not establish that lowering sensitivity improves this benchmark or reflects current user purpose.

related_work.title: [2] Positional Encoding Is Not the Same as Context
contributions: Distinguishes item-order information from temporal footprints in sequential recommendation.
limitations: Motivates positional controls but does not validate the proposed matched replacement protocol.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with exact metrics and change model ordering.
limitations: Does not invalidate the prescribed benchmark; full-catalog diagnostics remain auxiliary.

related_work.title: [4] Can LLM be a Personalized Judge?
contributions: Reports limited overall agreement with actual preferences and stronger agreement on high-certainty cases.
limitations: Does not supply preference labels or validate semantic judgments for these twenty training users.
